extracted.intended_audience: public company reporting officers, legal counsel, and compliance staff preparing SEC climate-related disclosures and economic analysts estimating compliance costs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for registrants to prepare and disclose climate-related information in SEC filings (including GHG emissions, targets and goals, scenario analysis, governance, risk management, XBRL tagging, and related assurance) and the Commission's methods/assumptions for estimating compliance costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and report Scopes 1, 2, and some Scope 3 emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants should measure and report Scope 1, Scope 2, and at least some Scope 3 emissions where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters and some companies explicitly state they measure and report Scopes 1, 2, and some Scope 3 emissions. Where registrants use consultants and engineering disciplines with GHG emissions reporting expertise, the Commission assumes costs of measuring these scopes may be included in reported costs. The Commission also notes some registrants may not include these costs in their reported figures to remain conservative in cost estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of targets and goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants should disclose targets and goals related to climate (e.g., net-zero commitments, low‑carbon financing goals) and progress toward them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sources often lack precise detail on what the targets-and-goals disclosure would consist of, making applicability to final rules uncertain. Some companies report progress toward low‑carbon financing and carbon‑neutrality goals and metrics like percentage renewable energy sourced and percentage energy reductions year-over-year. The Commission applied conservative assumptions when estimating whether reported company costs include setting targets and goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenario analysis disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants should disclose scenario analyses used to assess climate-related risks and impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission references scenario analysis as a component of the disclosure obligations (see section IV.C.3.b.iv) but notes available commenter sources do not always provide sufficient detail to determine cost applicability; the Commission nonetheless uses available sources to inform compliance cost estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance disclosure regarding climate-related risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the governance structures, oversight, and roles related to climate-related risks and disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governance disclosure is one of the core disclosure categories (along with strategy and risk management). The FCA and BEIS rules showed reductions from initial year to subsequent years for governance disclosure costs; the Commission used a median 44% reduction to estimate initial versus subsequent year costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of climate-related risks that materially impact strategy, business model, and outlook
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose material climate-related risks and how those risks have materially affected or could affect the registrant's strategy, business model, and outlook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a central disclosure category; costs associated with producing these disclosures were modeled using analogous reductions from other rules (FCA/BEIS) and incorporated into initial and ongoing cost estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk management disclosure for climate-related risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe processes used to identify, assess, and manage climate-related risks, and how those processes are integrated into overall risk management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is another core disclosure area. The Commission considered commenter input on the operational feasibility and potential costs of designing new controls and systems to capture climate risk information when estimating burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material expenditures directly related to climate-related activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose material expenditures directly related to climate-related activities as part of strategy, transition plans, and/or targets and goals, where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No commenters provided specific cost estimates for disclosure of material expenditures; the Commission applied conservative assumptions (estimating $327,000 first year and $183,000 annually thereafter) and reasoned that registrants will likely be tracking these expenditures under financial statement disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational boundaries for GHG accounting (may differ from financial statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the organizational boundaries used for GHG emissions disclosures; the final rules allow these boundaries to differ from those used in financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters noted differences between California laws and the proposed rules in organizational boundary definitions. The Commission recognizes such differences reduce potential cost mitigation via overlap and explicitly allows registrants to use different boundaries than in their financial statements (see accompanying text and supra note 1034).

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of disclosure (annual reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate-related disclosures under the final rules are required on an annual basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters contrasted California laws that require biennial reporting; the Commission notes that requirements like the Climate Related Financial Risk Act differ in frequency, and that such differences can increase administrative costs for coordinating compliance with multiple regimes. The final rules require annual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inline XBRL tagging for climate disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Tag the new climate-related disclosures in Inline XBRL to support consistency, comparability, and machine-readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters (e.g., Impact Capital Managers; Climate Advisers) indicated Inline XBRL tagging will elicit more consistent, comparable, and reliable disclosure and facilitate investor analyses. The Commission cites empirical literature on XBRL adoption and market impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance of climate-related disclosures (limited vs reasonable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may seek assurance over their emissions disclosures; assurance levels (limited vs reasonable) affect costs and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One commenter (Salesforce) estimated obtaining reasonable (vs limited) assurance would increase costs by $1–$3 million. The Commission acknowledges commenters suggesting many registrants will seek assurance from registered public accounting firms, which could increase assurance costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Securities-law liability for climate disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate-related disclosures filed with or incorporated into SEC filings are subject to securities-law liability, including Section 11 liability when included in or incorporated into a Securities Act registration statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission notes these disclosures are subject to heightened liability, which may affect registrant behavior and perceptions of credibility compared to voluntary sustainability reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use GAAP/financial-reporting principles for climate-related financial impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounting for climate-related financial impacts should follow U.S. GAAP where applicable, including recognition, measurement, and disclosure rules for impairments, contingencies, and related line items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters observed GAAP line items do not capture certain climate impacts (e.g., lost revenues under GAAP). The Commission references specific GAAP rules (17 CFR 210.14‑02 series) and examples where events (e.g., destruction by fire/storm) would be accounted for and disclosed under U.S. GAAP if material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and aggregate line-item financial impacts attributable to climate (degree of causation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must consider and, where applicable, count financial impacts that could plausibly be attributable to climate risks or events, determine the degree of climate causation associated with each impact, and aggregate them to determine if they meet materiality thresholds (e.g., 1% threshold) for each financial statement line item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argued this would require counting every plausible climate-attributable impact and determining causation; the Commission cites 17 CFR 210.14‑02 and recognizes operational challenges raised by commenters but applies the existing framework for determining material impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tagging/reporting historical period emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide historical emissions data for prior periods as part of disclosures where required or practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters (e.g., Autodesk) noted compiling necessary historical data may be prohibitively costly. The Commission acknowledges the potential cost and operational burden of compiling data for historical periods in its cost analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure metrics and monitoring/data quality (e.g., carbon abatement, water conservation, renewable energy %, energy reductions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report metrics related to climate performance such as carbon abatement, renewable energy percentages, water conservation, and year-over-year energy reductions, and report monitoring and data quality practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies described gathering metrics/data related to carbon abatement, renewable energy, water conservation, and incurring expenses for monitoring and data quality. The Commission used descriptions of these activities to inform assumptions about whether reported costs included setting targets/goals and metrics collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external consultants and allocation of consultant costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Where registrants engage external sustainability or emissions consultants, disclose methodology and account for external costs; when estimating compliance costs, the Commission distinguishes costs directly attributable to TCFD-related disclosures from broader sustainability consultant costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission noted commenters often did not tie consultant costs explicitly to TCFD; therefore, in cost estimation it used TCFD disclosure costs where directly relevant and omitted consultant costs when the portion attributable to TCFD could not be reliably determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: TCFD/CDP alignment and CDP-to-TCFD cost ratio assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures should be aligned with the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD); the Commission assumes a 4-to-9 staff-time ratio (CDP questionnaire takes 4 months, TCFD disclosures 9 months) when mapping CDP-based cost inputs to TCFD/SEC disclosure requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission cites letters noting it takes a designated number of staff four months to complete the CDP questionnaire and nine months to complete TCFD disclosures; it incorporates the 4-to-9 ratio into cost estimation where CDP data are used to infer TCFD burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-estimation conventions (use medians; burden-hour unit costs; reporting cost fraction)
rubrics_metrics.description: When estimating compliance costs, the Commission uses medians rather than means, assumes internal burden hours cost $444/hour and external burden hours cost $600/hour, and assumes reporting costs are approximately 10% of the cost of undertaking associated data-gathering activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission explains medians are less sensitive to outliers. BEIS estimated reporting costs were ~9.4% of annual data gathering costs; the Commission similarly assumes ~10% to estimate reporting burdens. These assumptions are applied throughout the cost-estimation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial-year versus subsequent-year cost adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that certain components of compliance costs may be higher in the initial year and decline in subsequent years; apply an adjustment factor (the Commission used a median 44% reduction based on FCA and BEIS rules) to estimate first-year versus ongoing costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FCA and BEIS rules reflected 56% and 32% reductions respectively from initial to subsequent years for provisions of interest; the Commission used the median (44%) to estimate initial costs. This adjustment is applied for governance, strategy, risk management, and related disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for overlapping/regulatory coordination with state/international regimes
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether compliance with other disclosure regimes (e.g., California laws, Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act) reduces or complicates costs through overlap or differences in scope, frequency, or organizational boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argued overlap with California laws could reduce costs; the Commission recognized differences (organizational boundaries, reporting frequency) that may reduce mitigation potential. The final rules allow some boundary differences, but coordination may create additional administrative costs.
